conviction_note: abs_move 9.0 (option event-implied 9.32 on a 51%-wide ATM spread; own median 7.15; a FY guide update under a new CEO is likely), p_up 56: a mild up lean from management's own July statement of possible Section 301 upside to the outlook, an unused ~$650m cash pile against a ~$1.17bn market cap, and a short base that doubled to ~18.6% of shares since mid-August, offset by Q3's dependence on ~200bp gross-margin expansion after Q2 missed management's own GM forecast by 80bp and by new-CEO reset risk. The findings sum (+2.8) is larger than the scaled number (+1.08) because the sign of the reaction is uncertain on a name whose big moves (-20%, -20%, +12%) all came on guidance, not on beats.
bar: Company Q3 guide (31 Jul 2026): net sales ~$750m, adj. operating income ~$50m, adj. EPS ~$0.85 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060822/000106082226000108/cri-ex991q22026.htm). MarketBeat consensus (19 Oct 2026): EPS $0.894, revenue $751.49m, FY26 EPS $3.28 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-carters-cri-set-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/). The Street sits ~$0.04 above the Q3 EPS guide, and its FY EPS of $3.28 is above the company's FY guide (high-single to low-double-digit decline from $3.47, i.e. about $3.05-3.19). So some tariff upside is already in estimates. The revenue bar is ~$750-751m from both sources.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/cri/shortinterest): 6,812,373 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 5.16 days to cover, 18.6% of shares outstanding (not free float). That is down from 7,570,539 at 09-30 but up from 3,163,032 at 08-14, so the short base doubled while the stock fell from $39.06 (Aug 12) to $29.03 (Sep 16; Yahoo daily bars). It is now $32.59 and 26.5% off its 52-week high. The baseline's 25-delta skew is null (no reading). Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.98. The option-implied event move is 9.32%, but the ATM spread is 51% of mid, so it is indicative only. A crowded and recently built short means negatives are shrunk and a clean print has a squeeze mechanism.

findings.finding: On the 31 Jul Q2 call, CFO Westenberger said that if the Section 301 rates (10-12.5% above baseline, replacing Section 122 from 24 Jul) hold, 'we may have some upside to our earnings outlook', and that gross tariff exposure fell from ~$200m to 'something along the lines of $75m'. No new Section 301 overcapacity tariffs on apparel had been announced through late October. A Q3/FY guide raise on tariffs is therefore plausible. The FY guide is a high-single to low-double-digit EPS decline (~$3.05-3.19), against Street FY EPS of $3.28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every large CRI move in the baseline came on guidance: Jul 2025 -19.7% (guidance suspended), Feb 2026 -20.3% (FY26 guide), May 2026 +11.7% (Q1 and new CEO). The Q2 2026 EPS beat ($0.26 vs ~$0.06 consensus) with the guide reaffirmed bought only +2.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Street FY EPS of $3.28 is already above the guide range, so the market expects some raise. If the raise were fully priced, the stock would not have fallen 26% after the call while the short base doubled; it sits near $32.6 against a $39 consensus target. What is unpriced is the size of the raise, which management refused to give.
findings.independence: Tariff rates and the overcapacity probe are still pending: https://www.dfdl.com/insights/legal-and-tax-updates/us-section-301-tariffs-asean-implications/ and https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/07/us-administration-rebuilds-global-tariff-program-under-section-301. These show rates unchanged at 10/12.5% since 24 Jul. This finding shares the call transcript with the gross-margin and capital findings.

findings.finding: Carter's held $653.6m of cash at 4 Jul 2026 (Q2 release) against a market cap of about $1.15-1.17bn, and bought back no stock in H1. On the Q2 call the CFO said 'I have no interest in having an inefficient balance sheet' and tied 'the time to perhaps do something with the cash' to the new CEO's planning season. A buyback or capital-return announcement with Q3 is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback announcement in the baseline window. The dividend was cut in 2025 (Stockopedia 'dividend cut' item), and it was a negative.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades at about 5.9x P/E with roughly 55% of its market cap in cash, so no buyback is being given credit. If it were priced, the shares would not have fallen 26% from mid-August on a reaffirmed guide. Management also said cash would fall on H2 inventory, the ~$30m tax on the refund and interest, so timing is uncertain.
findings.independence: The CFO quote comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978314-20260808), which is shared with the tariff finding. The cash figure comes from the 8-K exhibit.

findings.finding: Short interest doubled into the print: 3.16m shares on 14 Aug, 7.57m on 30 Sep and 6.81m on 15 Oct (18.6% of shares outstanding, 5.16 days to cover). Over the same span the stock fell from $39 to $29 with no company 8-K explaining it, and it has since recovered to $32.6. A crowded, recently built short gives a clean print a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No short-interest-driven reaction is in the baseline. The May 2026 +11.7% came when the stock was depressed after the Feb -20%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own state, not information it lacks. What is filed here is the asymmetry: a short of about 5 days' volume built into a quarter the company guided to +$11m of operating income y/y. If shorts had already covered, SI would be back near 3m.
findings.independence: Price path from Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CRI?range=4mo&interval=1d). Form 4 tax-withholding prices of $39.96 (8 Aug) and $39.06 (12 Aug) confirm the mid-August level: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1060822/000106082226000117/0001060822-26-000117.txt

findings.finding: Census advance retail sales for clothing and accessory stores were $26,327m / $26,486m / $26,478m for Jul / Aug / Sep 2026, against $25,254m / $25,400m / $25,222m a year earlier. That is +4.5% y/y for the quarter and +5.0% in September, the month management said carries the majority of Q3 sales. BofA card spending per household was +6.2% y/y in September. This supports Carter's US Retail, which was guided to low-single-digit Q3 growth after flat July comps.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 US Retail comps of +5.1% came with a +2.1% reaction. Retail beats alone have not moved this stock much.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro proxy, not company data. Census apparel is broad (teen and adult), and Carter's has a heavy mix of baby and wholesale. A broad series is public, so this is small. It matters because management called Q3 'wait-and-see' with September weighted heavily.
findings.independence: Proxy. BofA Consumer Checkpoint Oct 2026 (https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/consumer-checkpoint-october-2026.html) shows September card spending +6.2% y/y, with lower-income households recovering. It is a different source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: The Q3 guide depends on gross margin expanding just under 200bp against a weaker wholesale channel. In Q2, gross margin came in about 80bp below management's own forecast because of Retail discounting. Management moderated H2 pricing assumptions, citing 'price resistance', and said some wholesale customers were 'more conservative' on H2 inventory after Q2 pulled Q3 shipments forward. Wholesale partners were soft in May-Jul: Target said apparel 'hardly grew' and was below expectations, and Kohl's children's net sales were -0.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin- and cash-driven disappointments produced Feb 2026 -20.3% and Apr 2025 -11.4%. Those came with guide cuts.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly inside the guide already: Q3 wholesale was guided down high single digits, which is why this is sized small. The unpriced part is whether retail promotions again cost GM against plan. The stock's 26% fall suggests some of this is feared.
findings.independence: Target Q2 (https://fashionunited.com/news/business/target-reports-5-3-percent-sales-growth-in-q2-as-apparel-and-core-categories-expand/2026081974159) and the Kohl's 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000885639/000119312526381893/kss-20260801.htm) cover May-Jul, which overlaps Carter's Q2, not Q3. Both are counterparty proxies.

findings.finding: New CEO Sharon Price John (since 15 Jun) said on the Q2 call that she had not yet sat with the board and was 'reticent' to lay out next steps, with the company 'in our planning season with a new leader'. On 15 Sep Carter's launched its first logo change since 2000 with a multi-year 'Watch Them Glow' campaign, with retail, product and packaging elements planned for 2027. The first full-quarter call under a new CEO risks an investment-heavy reset of 2027 expectations, through higher demand-creation SG&A.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 -20.3% came on an FY guide calling for an EPS decline driven by investment and tariffs. That was the only full-year framing event in the window.
findings.why_not_priced: This is inference, not a document: no company number says SG&A will rise in 2027. The stock fell 4.4% on 15 Sep, the day of the rebrand, which suggests part is already in. If a reset were fully expected, Street FY EPS would not sit above the guide.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo cut its target from $42 to $30 on 12 Oct (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-carters-cri-set-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/). The reason is not given. The CEO quotes come from the call transcript, which is shared with the other findings.

findings.finding: Wells Fargo cut its CRI target from $42 to $30 (equal weight) on 12 Oct 2026, putting a bear-ish target near spot shortly before the print, while the consensus target is still $39.38. A lower sell-side bar makes an in-line print easier to read as relief.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and the cut itself is priced. What is filed is that it lowers the effective bar for the reaction. One aggregator carries it, the reasoning is unknown, and a search result disputed its date, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Direct competitor The Children's Place reported May-Jul 2026 comps of -16.7% and net sales of -18.9%, with $7.2m of cash and $79.7m of liquidity, and fell 22.9% on 15 Sep. Over a similar period Carter's US Retail comped +5.1%, which points to share shifting to Carter's in kids' specialty retail while the competitor is liquidity-constrained.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy, and PLCE's problems are largely idiosyncratic (liquidity, store openings). It is public since mid-September. Its read-through to Carter's Q3 is inference, so it is small.

outside_window.finding: The USTR Section 301 structural-overcapacity investigation (launched March 2026, covering 16 economies including textiles and apparel) is still open and likely to add tariffs. Any action is undated and would hit Carter's sourcing costs in 2027.

baseline_tension: The skew is null, so there is no option-market direction to fight. The 20-day run-up is +2.8% and the 5-day is -4.0%, after a 26% drawdown since mid-August into a crowded short. The mild up lean runs with the short-squeeze asymmetry, but the stock's history of 20% falls on guidance keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide or estimates): the Section 301 upside is partly in Street FY EPS above the guide, so +1.5 becomes +1.2.

Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0) together with lesson 7 (a crowded short is a mechanism): the positioning finding is trimmed from +1.5 to +1.0, and the drawdown itself is merged into it rather than counted.
Lessons 6 and 7: the gross-margin/wholesale negative is mostly inside the guided HSD wholesale decline and sits against an 18.6% short, so -1.0 becomes -0.6.
Lesson 7: the new-CEO reset negative is inference against a crowded short, so -1.0 becomes -0.7.
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the capital-return finding goes from +1.0 to +0.8, since the timing is not stated and the CFO flagged cash outflows.
abs_move_pct, p_up and print_vs_bar are unchanged: the lessons moved the findings, not the scaled measurement (core step 4).
